data.one_liner: Dart implementation of Rust's Result monad type and anyhow crate for error handling.
data.what_it_does: Provides a Result monad type and error context capabilities, allowing functions to return errors without throwing exceptions. Developers can add context or downcast errors to inspect root causes.
use_when: You want predictable control flow without throwing exceptions.
You need to attach contextual information to errors as they bubble up the call stack.
avoid_when: Your project standardizes heavily on Dart's built-in try-catch exception handling.
You require detailed third-party integrations that exclusively rely on standard Dart exceptions.
strengths: Enables idiomatic Rust-style error handling in Dart.
Allows adding context and chaining errors to trace exact issues.
weaknesses: Requires adopting a Result monad paradigm instead of traditional exceptions.
Downcasting underlying errors is intended to be used sparingly.
